notes:
User is meal-prepping healthy lunches and recently bought a new Instant Pot and Air Fryer. They enjoy Korean-inspired dishes and make-ahead soups/stews. Previously requested a detailed Instant Pot Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) recipe; planned adaptation uses boneless skinless chicken breast, pressure cooks 10–12 minutes, checks for 165°F/74°C, and starts with 1 tablespoon gochugaru, adjusting to taste. Sempio/Koko gochugaru and Sunchang/Chongga gochujang were recommended.

User enjoys bean- and lentil-based healthy meals, especially ideas similar to chili con carne. They considered a Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl with onions, bell pepper, garlic, brown rice, avocado, and lime, served with Air Fryer sweet potato fries and a refreshing fruit salad dessert. Air Fryer fries: preferably starchy Russet/Idaho potatoes, cut uniformly about ½ inch thick, soak 30 minutes, dry thoroughly, lightly oil, air-fry at 400°F/200°C for 12–15 minutes in batches, shake halfway, season after cooking; avoid overcrowding. Fruit salad may include berries, grapes, kiwi, pineapple, lime, and mint.

For Cuban bowl leftovers, refrigerate promptly in shallow airtight containers at 40°F/4°C or below, within 2 hours, and use within 3–4 days; freeze portions for longer storage, ideally after cooling quickly, in airtight freezer containers/bags. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Rice and cooked vegetables generally keep well frozen, but texture is best when slightly moist; add a splash of broth or lime if dry.

For sweet potato fries, do not store at room temperature or in the pantry. Refrigerate only briefly (preferably same day) in an airtight container lined with paper towel, though they will soften. For longer storage, freeze fully cooked fries in a single layer, then transfer to airtight freezer bags/containers. Re-crisp from frozen in Air Fryer or oven at 400°F/200°C, shaking/baking as needed. Discard fries with spoilage signs. Be practical and encouraging; user values healthy, easy, meal-prep-friendly guidance.
trajectory:
User is meal-prepping healthy lunches and recently bought a new Instant Pot. They are interested in make-ahead soups and stews, especially Korean-inspired dishes. They asked for a detailed Instant Pot Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) recipe, including ingredient quantities, sauté/pressure-cooking instructions, and Korean condiment recommendations. Previous recommendations included Sempio or Koko gochugaru and Sunchang or Chongga gochujang, available at Asian markets or online.

Planned adaptation:
- Use boneless, skinless chicken breast cut into bite-size pieces instead of thighs/drumsticks.
- Reduce high-pressure cooking time from 20 minutes to about 10–12 minutes, checking that internal temperature reaches 165°F/74°C.
- Chicken breast may be slightly drier; suggest a breast-and-thigh combination if a moist texture is preferred.
- Use only 1 tablespoon gochugaru/chili flakes initially, then taste and adjust; omit it or add small amounts later if needed. The original recipe also has 2 tablespoons gochujang, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, black pepper, chicken broth, potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, sesame oil, and optional green onions.
- Suggested process: sauté chicken and set aside; sauté aromatics, then briefly sauté vegetables; whisk seasonings into the pot; add broth and chicken; pressure cook; natural release 10 minutes, then quick-release remaining pressure; season, garnish, and serve with rice/noodles and optionally kimchi.
- User is excited to begin preparing the ingredients and values guidance on spice level and doneness. Be encouraging and practical if they report cooking results or ask follow-ups.
